time._offsetComment: Time offset: what was originally decimal time 3:18:86 is now 0:000:000 (= 3×20736 + 18×144 + 86 = 64886 units)

historicalHolidays.name: 🔭 Einstein Day — General Relativity
historicalHolidays.desc: Marking the presentation of the field equations of general relativity (November 25, 1915) — by Albert Einstein. The theory describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime and transformed the foundations of modern physics.

historicalHolidays.name: 🍎 Newton Day
historicalHolidays.desc: Marking the publication of Principia Mathematica (July 5, 1687) — by Isaac Newton. The book formulated the three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation, laying the foundation for classical mechanics.

historicalHolidays.name: 🔭 Galileo Day
historicalHolidays.desc: Marking the publication of Sidereus Nuncius (March 13, 1610) — by Galileo Galilei. The book described telescopic observations that discovered the moons of Jupiter, supporting the Copernican heliocentric theory.

historicalHolidays.name: 🎓 Plato Day
historicalHolidays.desc: Marking the traditional birthday of Plato — according to ancient tradition (Diogenes Laërtius) he was born on the seventh day of the month of Thargelion, the birthday of Apollo (roughly corresponding to May 21, circa 428 BCE). Plato founded the Academy in Athens, the first institution of organized higher learning in the West, where his student Aristotle was educated.

historicalHolidays.name: 🐢 Darwin Day
historicalHolidays.desc: Marking the publication of On the Origin of Species (November 24, 1859) — by Charles Darwin. The book presented the theory of evolution by natural selection, transforming the scientific understanding of the diversity of life on Earth.

historicalHolidays.name: ☢️ Marie Curie Day
historicalHolidays.desc: Marking the discovery of radium (December 26, 1898) — by Marie Curie, together with her husband Pierre. Marie Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, and the first person to win two Nobel Prizes in two different fields of science — physics and chemistry.

historicalHolidays.name: 🧫 Fleming Day
historicalHolidays.desc: Marking the discovery of penicillin (September 3, 1928) — by Alexander Fleming. The British researcher accidentally discovered the first antibiotic, which sparked a medical revolution and saved millions of lives.

historicalHolidays.name: 📐 Archimedes Day
historicalHolidays.desc:
Marking Pi Day — 3 days, as the nearest whole number to the constant π.

Archimedes of Syracuse approximated π, discovered the principle of buoyancy ("Eureka!"), and calculated areas and volumes using the method of exhaustion, one of the founding fathers of mechanics and mathematics in antiquity.

aristoHoliday.name: 🏛️ Aristotle Day
aristoHoliday.desc: Marking the birthday of Aristotle (384 BCE) — a Greek philosopher, father of logic, biology, physics, and more. Student of Plato and teacher of Alexander the Great.
